_readme: Edit this file to add your targets. Delete any you don't need. interval = seconds between checks (normal). hot_interval kicks in near drop_time or when you send /hot in Telegram.

targets.name: Ticketmaster — Coldplay
targets._note: BEST OPTION for TM. Free API key from developer.ticketmaster.com — no scraping, no blocking. Swap YOUR_KEY and the keyword.

targets.name: Tiket.com — event page
targets._note: Tiket.com is a Next.js site. The whole page state sits in a __NEXT_DATA__ JSON blob — the bot digs it out automatically. Find the right path by viewing source once.

targets.name: Loket — event
targets._note: Watch for the buy button appearing. Open the page in Safari, tap Share > find the exact button text first (e.g. 'BELI TIKET', 'Pilih Tiket').

targets.name: Loket — sold out watch (restock)
targets._note: Opposite direction: fires when SOLD OUT disappears. Great for catching released/cancelled seats.

targets.name: Ticket2U — event
targets._note: Plain HTML site. ignore_pattern strips timestamps/CSRF tokens that change every load and would cause false alarms.

targets.name: Shopee — flash sale item
targets._note: Get item_id and shop_id from the product URL: shopee.co.id/…-i.SHOPID.ITEMID. Shopee blocks hard — if you see 403 in logs, drop back to watching the normal product page with a 'changed' rule and a slower interval.

targets.name: Tokopedia — product
targets._note: Tokopedia's real API is GraphQL/POST and locked down. Watching the public product page for the stock text flipping is more reliable. Confirm the exact wording on the page first — 'Stok habis' vs 'Produk tidak tersedia'.

targets.name: TEST — GitHub status
targets._note: Leave this on for the first run so you can confirm the pipes work end to end. Turn it off after.
